address_spaces.name: I/O
address_spaces.notes: Sixteen small windows of 16 MB fill offsets 0x0000_0000 to 0x0fff_ffff, widget N at N times 16 MB. Seven big windows of 512 MB start at 0x2000_0000. Small window 0 and big window 6 are two views of the same widget, and both decode: Linux reads widget 0's identification register through the small window by its raw address, OpenBSD reaches the same device through the big window, so both paths have to work. See docs/datasheets/address-map.md for the small-window-0 reversal history.

machine.name: Origin 2000 deskside
machine.notes: Four node boards, each with two processors and 256 MiB in two 128 MB banks, two Standard Routers, and a plain BaseIO (io6) in IO1, and no graphics, as a shipped Origin 2000 deskside has none. The Routers are the model's choice: SGI shipped three- and four-node desksides with a Router and a Star Router. The machine's nodes= property fits fewer node boards, in SGI's fill order: one takes no Router board and two a Null Router (007-3453-002 Figure 2-9). This is the eight-processor module, so node 1 reaches Crossbow 0 at widget 9, node 2 Crossbow 1 at widget A, node 3 Crossbow 0 at widget A and node 4 Crossbow 1 at widget 9. This is a selected population, not a captured machine inventory. The full processor mode word is not the full CP0 Config register; only the reviewed low 25 bits transfer. Stock image configuration must agree and is never rewritten by descriptor generation.

variants.notes: Identity registers and cache clock corroborated as the same R10000/1 MiB assembly Origin 200 already catalogues (a real Origin 200 hinv reports "Rev 2.6"; boot-logs records this as the same variant on both products).

Reset mode cleared by the independent firmware-configuration review (candidate 7a0508cb6f18b5d8441b8e0dca30f8e386d503fd, docs/reviews/origin2000-firmware-configuration-review-20260905.md) recomputed from IRIX 6.5.7 configuration data and reconciled with the public processor manual and SGI service procedure; docs/datasheets/origin2000-cache-configuration.md records the clearance. This is not the product's selected default (that is 180 MHz/1 MiB); no product here authors it. Identity registers and cache clock for this SKU are not established by any held source and are absent here.

space_selection.notes: Two bits the processor drives beside the address, not part of it. All four spaces decode to the same 40-bit physical address and the attribute is what tells them apart. Emulator carrier addresses are target implementation metadata and do not belong in this shared hardware layer.
